title: Mycobacterium ulcerans DNA Detection in Environmental Samples by Real-Time PCR
author: Issaka Maman1
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.pb7dirn

steps.title: Homogenize plant, soil, and fecal samples
steps.instruction: Prepare soil, plant, and animal feces samples for DNA extraction using a FastPrep-24 instrument.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 200µl of each sample to a lysing matrix E tube (MP Biomedicals) containing MT Buffer and sodium phosphate buffer (MP Biomedicals).
Homogenize on the FastPrep-24 instrument for 40s at speed setting 6.0.
Centrifuge the Matrix E tubes at 14000xg for 10 minutes to pellet debris.

steps.title: Process biofilm and water samples
steps.instruction: Prepare biofilm and water samples for DNA extraction.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 200µl of sample into a Matrix E tube.
Centrifuge at 14000xg for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Extract DNA
steps.instruction: Extract DNA from the collected supernatants of the processed samples.

substeps.instruction: Collect the supernatant after centrifugation.
Extract DNA using the FastDNA® Spin Kit for Soil (MP Biomedicals) according to the manufacturer's recommendations.
Include one negative extraction control (sterile water) for each extraction batch to monitor cross-contamination.

steps.title: Perform quantitative IS2404-qPCR
steps.instruction: Conduct the first qPCR run targeting the IS2404 insertion sequence to identify potential M. ulcerans DNA.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a calibration curve using serial dilutions of DNA from a synthetic M. ulcerans Transposase pMUM001 (58 bp) gene.

Prepare a reaction mixture consisting of 3µl extracted DNA and 22µl master mix. The master mix must contain: 0.5µl IPC DNA, 2.5µl IPC master mix, 1.25µl IS2404 forward primer, 1.25µl IS2404 reverse primer, 1.25µl IS2404 probe, 2.75µl water, and 12.5µl TaqMan Environmental Master mix 2.0.
Include an internal positive control (IPC), a no template control (NTC), and a positive control in quadruplicate.
Run the reaction on an ABI 7300 machine using these conditions: 50°C for 2 minutes, 95°C for 15 minutes, and 40 cycles of (95°C for 15 seconds and 60°C for 60 seconds).
Identify inhibited samples (where neither IPC nor IS2404 amplified) and re-test them after a 10-fold dilution in RNase/DNase free water.

steps.title: Perform semi-quantitative IS2606-qPCR
steps.instruction: Test samples that were positive for IS2404 in a second qPCR run targeting the IS2606 insertion sequence.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a master mix containing: 1.25µl IS2606 forward primer, 1.25µl IS2606 reverse primer, 1.25µl IS2606 probe, 5.75µl water, and 12.5µl TaqMan Environmental Master mix 2.0 (do not use IPC).
Combine 3µl of DNA extract with 22µl of the master mix.
Run the reaction using the same amplification conditions as the IS2404-PCR.

steps.title: Perform semi-quantitative KR-B qPCR
steps.instruction: Analyze samples that tested positive for both IS2404 and IS2606 for the presence of the mycolactone gene, KR-B.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a reaction mixture consisting of 5µl DNA extract and 20µl of master mix.
Use the same master mix components (excluding IPC) and amplification conditions as the IS2606-PCR, substituting the IS2606 primers/probe with KR-B specific primers/probe.
Test all samples in duplicate.

steps.title: Interpret results
steps.instruction: Determine if the environmental sample is positive for M. ulcerans based on the following criteria:

substeps.instruction: The sample must be positive for IS2404, IS2606, and KR-B gene in replicates.
The threshold cycle (Ct) for the KR-B gene must be < 40.
The difference in cycle threshold (ΔCt) between IS2404 and IS2606 must be < 7.
